analysis:
Examined the 4 changed files: the ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl refresh hook, the new SelectedModelPlacementPolicy file, the capacity tick hook, and the model-unload hooks. No concrete security regression found.

1) ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift:76 copies `config.backend.enabledModels` from the owner-controlled local config into `savedEnabledModels`. This is local operator state read with `ConfigManager.load`. It does not alter consent, revision, lease or control validation, so TB-011 and A-016 serving-authorization boundaries are unchanged. Coordinator-supplied Autopilot control is still checked for revision, session length and expiry at lines 110-112.

2) ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift (new) releases an Autopilot adoption outside the operator's selection. The release applies only when the model is unheld, unpinned, the adoption is valid, and it is excluded from eviction solely because it serves requests (lines 25-27). The release time is 600s after the hold or the wait start, never earlier than the minimum dwell or the per-model lease (lines 28-33). `releaseAdoptionForSelectedModelRecovery` removes the adoption, withdraws it so no new requests are admitted, lets in-flight requests finish, then republishes the snapshot and sends a heartbeat (lines 41-48). This narrows exposure and does not widen routing. A-018 availability impact is limited by the hold, dwell and lease guards. Any locally controlled input would need `selectedModelRecovery` and `isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction`, which are outside the supplied evidence.

3) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 adds `checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue()` to the periodic tick. ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift:1145-1149 and 1216 call `selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue` after unload/retire. These are scheduling triggers only. Complexity or recursion in `checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue` (not supplied, in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery) and its interaction with load admission and drain remain unverified.

No prompt data, keys or attestation paths are touched. The T-041 cache surface is unaffected. Remaining integration questions: how the unseen `selectedModelRecovery` and `checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue` implementations bound eviction and reload cycles (T-010/T-029 availability).
